answer: A verifiable delay function protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate sequential modular squarings to mint identity tickets. Peers verify these proofs across a trellis of state checkpoints in the agent orchard, leaving uncertified nodes on an untrusted island. An attacker incurs a non-negotiable cost of elapsed wall-clock time per identity. However, this creates high registration latency and remains vulnerable to ASIC acceleration.
